A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MIG-Vis on the same macaque IT recordings. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and revised material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-synthesis comparisons, latent-selectivity analyses, neural reconstruction ablations and disentanglement measurements in Figures 4–7 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthesis and reconstruction results, including revised visual comparisons, latent-subset reconstruction in Table 3 and additional analyses in Figures 8–10.

M1.justification: The central probing procedure changes from guiding a reference image toward another image's latent group to guiding toward an additive perturbation of its own latent group, z_tilde_g = z_g + gamma*1. v2 supports both perturbation directions and separates the diffusion-guidance coefficient eta. The VAE, InfoNCE objective and DDIM backbone remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two-macaque IT dataset with 5,760 grayscale stimuli spanning eight object categories. Revised exemplar choices, latent traversal and parameter sweeps remain within the existing neural reconstruction and semantic-probing tasks.

E2.justification: Figure 5 removes AP-LR, the BrainDIVE-derived comparator, while retaining SLT, AP-CFG and the no-MI ablation. v2 describes the no-MI comparator explicitly through probabilistic-encoder likelihood guidance rather than the earlier brief activation-guidance description. Tables 1–2 retain their VAE comparators.

E3.justification: v1 varies diffusion-guidance strength over {2,5,10}; v2 tests latent offsets {-10,-5,5,10} under the revised probing procedure. New evaluations vary group count G=3/5, InfoNCE sample count B=8/16/32 and latent subsets used for reconstruction. Reported M1/M2 channel counts also reverse from 110/58 to 58/110, without establishing that recordings or experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity analyses for group count and InfoNCE sample count, supervised-versus-unsupervised latent reconstruction in Table 3, and trial-level reconstruction checks in Figure 8. Fine-grained probing cases are revised, including replacing the Group 3 table example with a strawberry. v1 Appendix C's additional reference-to-target case studies are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means and standard deviations in Table 1 and five-run averages with uncertainties in Table 2. New Table 3 uses the existing plus/minus reporting style without specifying a new statistical procedure, seed policy or increased run count.

E6.justification: The central qualitative results in Figures 4–7 are substantially revised. For example, v1 describes AP-CFG as unable to uncover rotation, whereas v2 reports reasonable rotation under the changed probing conditions; this is not a same-setting performance gain. Tables 1–2 remain numerically identical. New Table 3 reports full-latent R² values of 76.13% and 71.82% for M1/M2, alongside subset results and new appendix plots.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds the mathematical perturbation specification z_tilde_g = z_g + gamma*1 with gamma drawn from U(-a,a). The VAE evidence bound, MI definition, InfoNCE bound, score relationship and Appendix A.2 clean-image derivation otherwise remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the principal claims: MIG-Vis combines group-disentangled neural representations with MI-guided deterministic diffusion to reveal pose, inter-category and intra-category selectivity in macaque IT. The first-work claim and contribution of probing within-group semantic structure also remain.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the earlier face/table-to-pear manifold-path explanation with a distinction between globally consistent pose semantics and locally curved, category-dependent content manifolds. It also develops a new argument that encoder-likelihood guidance is one-sided and weaker than MI guidance. These substantially revise the mechanisms proposed to explain the visual results.

D1.justification: The repository pointer changes from yulewang97/MIG-Vis to BRAINML-GT/MIG-Vis, while v1's explicit data-access and supplementary-ZIP statement disappears. Appendix A.1's training and hardware details are unchanged. The revised inference description introduces a separate diffusion-guidance coefficient eta without providing its numerical setting.

R1.justification: v2 adds Whiteway et al. (2021) when discussing direct decoding and Li et al. (2023) for importance sampling. It removes Yang Song et al.'s score-based SDE reference while retaining the DDIM paper. Positioning against decoder-based visualization becomes more explicit, but the overall novelty claim remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, latter introduction, Section 3.2, baseline discussion and manifold interpretation receive substantial rewriting. The setup subsection is folded into Section 4, experimental subsections are renumbered, and appendix organization changes. Publication headers and an acknowledgement are also added or revised.

P2.justification: Figures 4–7 are redesigned around negative and positive traversal with a central original image, replacing the reference-to-target layouts. Figures 2 and 7 redraw the conceptual manifolds. The appendix gallery is replaced by reconstruction and sensitivity displays, and Table 3 is added, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful bidirectional probing, sensitivity tests and reconstruction diagnostics, but important new evidence is incompletely specified. Table 3 reports M2 full-latent R² of 71.82%, versus 81.86% in retained Table 2, without explaining the relationship between those evaluations. The newly separated guidance coefficient eta also lacks a numerical setting. These reporting gaps limit the benefits of the added analyses, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
